description: Rules R1 to R16 of the command adaptation map, as data. They are applied in order to the whole text of an ECC command when it is installed, and to its description. A rule has an id, the number of the map rule it belongs to (`rule`), a regular expression (`pattern`, with optional `flags` from i, m, s and u), a `replacement` (JavaScript replacement syntax: $1, $&), and a `why`. `commands` limits a rule to the named commands, and then `expect` is the number of times it must match in each of them, so a changed ECC file stops the plan instead of being half fixed. `append` names a snippet of snippets.json (S2 or S3) that is added once at the end of a command the rule has changed. {{commands}} in a pattern stands for the names of the ECC commands, {{uninstalledSkills}} for the skills of `uninstalledSkills` that the install does not have. Credit and license text is never rewritten, whatever the rules say. R3 (frontmatter) and S1 (the header) are done by the installer. R11, R12, R15 and R16 have no rewrite: a command that needs them is class B or C, and the lint keeps it out. Delete a rule to turn it off.

rules.pattern: Invoke the `(orch-[a-z-]+)` skill with `\$ARGUMENTS` as the (request|doc path)\.
rules.replacement: Load the `$1` skill: read `.kiro/skills/$1/SKILL.md` and `.kiro/skills/orch-pipeline/SKILL.md`, then follow them with `$ARGUMENTS` as the $2. At each gate, stop and wait for the user's reply. Never approve a gate yourself.
rules.why: In Kiro the instruction to invoke a skill did nothing: headless runs never read the skill and improvised the pipeline. The command now names the files to read, and keeps the gates.
